decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 offered read-later either as an item that “graduat[es] into your main collection” or “a label/view you flip on and off.” Client entry 4 selected the conforming behavior: “a status I can turn on or off while the bookmark remains in the same collection” and marking read must not delete or move it.
decisions.note: Specification exploration: the alternatives differed functionally, and the client selected the reference-conforming status model.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 presented a separate read-later space. Client entry 4 confirmed: “a separate view showing only unread items.”
decisions.note: Specification exploration: the recorded separate unread view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 presented entering a link in “Save a link” and adding it to the collection; client entry 6 approved the two-step capture flow.
decisions.note: Prototype review: URL-based saving conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 presented automatic title and description only. Client entry 6 supplied the missing metadata: “the site’s small icon” and “A preview image.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the initial metadata decision omitted two required collected fields.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 allowed reviewing and adjusting the auto-filled title or description before saving. Client entry 6 said, “The two-step save feels right.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: pre-save metadata editing conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 allowed typing “a tag or two” while saving; client entry 6 retained tags in the requested capture flow.
decisions.note: Prototype review: assigning multiple tags conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 listed card contents as title, address, description, note, and tags, omitting a favicon. Client entry 6 said the site’s icon should be “collected and shown so I can scan the list more easily.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the initial readability-first card omitted the required per-item favicon.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 stated the saved title is clickable and opens the link. Client entry 6 did not contest this behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: navigation to the original URL conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 presented the saved card as showing the note, and client entry 6 did not address formatting. Maker entry 33/round 17 later established the earlier behavior displayed raw symbols by saying notes “now” render formatting “instead of raw symbols.”
decisions.note: Initial prototype review: notes were displayed without Markdown rendering, but that difference passed unexpressed in the immediate response.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 presented tags and a note in the save form but no unread control. Client entry 6 responded, “I need a way to mark the bookmark as ‘read later’ while saving it.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the initial capture form omitted setting unread/read-later status.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 offered free tag typing without suggestions. Client entry 6 requested that “existing tags should be suggested.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: tag autocomplete was missing from the initial save flow.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 presented adding a link without duplicate handling. Client entry 6 required that re-saving an address “recognize the existing bookmark and let me edit that one rather than create a duplicate.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: duplicate-save convergence was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 presented collected site icon and page preview in addition to the existing title/description flow. Client entry 8 said the updated saving flow satisfied the request.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: automatic metadata collection conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 presented type-ahead matching and click-to-accept existing tags. Client entry 8 said this was “exactly what I pictured.”
decisions.note: Revised prototype: tag autocomplete conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 presented an existing-URL warning followed by editing the original in place. Client entry 8 approved “keeping a single copy.”
decisions.note: Revised prototype: duplicate saves converge on editing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 added a “Read later” switch during saving and a marker on the card. Client entry 8 approved both.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: setting unread status during save conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 presented search across title, description, note, tags, and site address. Client entry 10 explicitly approved searching title, description, note, and address.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the required full-text fields are covered; ordinary tag matching is an additional behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 did not state whether matching was case-insensitive. Client entry 10 expressed the expectation: “It should also ignore capitalization.” Later search presentations and approvals did not explicitly establish or dispose of case behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype/specification review: the requirement was expressed, but the record cannot independently establish the presented behavior or a specific resolution.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 presented ordinary word/tag-word search only. Client entry 10 requested that “#reference should mean the tag specifically” and combine with ordinary terms.
decisions.note: Prototype review: explicit #tag search was missing from the initial search language.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 presented simple word search. Client entry 10 added, “Quotation marks should find an exact phrase.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: exact-phrase search was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 presented only simple searches. Client entry 10 requested “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses” and quoted operator words as literal text.
decisions.note: Prototype review: Boolean operators, grouping, and literal-operator handling were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 11/round 6 presented exact #tag matching and implicit AND with ordinary words. Client entry 12 approved exact matching and the combinations.
decisions.note: Revised search prototype: tag syntax conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 11/round 6 presented quoted exact phrases; client entry 12 said quoted phrases behaved as expected.
decisions.note: Revised search prototype: exact-phrase matching conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 11/round 6 presented AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, and quoted operators as literal text. Client entry 12 approved all of these behaviors.
decisions.note: Revised search prototype: Boolean query behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 15 and 17/rounds 8–9 presented filtering by a tag bar and clickable card tags. Client entries 16 and 18 approved both and confirmed the list narrows to that tag.
decisions.note: Linked prototype choice and confirmation: both UI mechanisms implement the required specific-tag filter.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 15 and 17/rounds 8–9 presented tag browsing combined with the active text search. Client entries 16 and 18 required and then confirmed that both constraints remain visible and apply together.
decisions.note: Prototype review: combined tag and full-text filtering conforms to the reference rule.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19/round 10 presented controls to add an item to read later and turn that status off. Client entry 20 selected explicit verb buttons while preserving the same status behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: unread status can be toggled; the UI-choice preference is functionally equivalent.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19/round 10 presented a separate “Read later” tab. Client entry 20 said the tabs matched the desired separate views.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the unread-only view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19/round 10 presented “Mark as read” removing an item from Read later while retaining it in All. Client entry 20 called this “exactly the behaviour I wanted.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: marking read has the required effect.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 21/round 11 asked whether common URL variants should converge. Client entry 22 confirmed they should resolve to one existing bookmark.
decisions.note: Boundary review: URL normalization strengthens the conforming duplicate rule.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 21/round 11 presented newest-first ordering as the list order. Client entry 22 said it must not be the only order and requested sorting by at least date added and title.
decisions.note: Boundary review: a fixed newest-first order omitted user-selectable sorting.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 21/round 11 presented only newest-first ordering. Client entry 22 additionally required the preferred default to be remembered.
decisions.note: Boundary review: the initial list-order decision omitted the default-sort preference.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 21/round 11 proposed treating large-collection behavior as a later goal. Client entry 22 explicitly stated the missing expectation—“I’d eventually like control over how many bookmarks are displayed at once”—while saying later treatment was “acceptable.” Maker entry 25/round 13 consequently recorded item-count control for a future round.
decisions.note: Boundary review: the client surfaced the reference display-count expectation and initially accepted its deferral; this was later superseded by a new corrective decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 23/round 12 presented newest, oldest, title A–Z, and title Z–A. Client entry 24 retained all four options.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: selectable sort keys conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 23/round 12 presented a remembered sort choice across views and filters. Client entry 24 confirmed this met the default-sort expectation.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: remembered default sort conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 declared the whole goal covered but only mentioned editing when a duplicate was re-saved. Client entry 26 required editing address, title, description, tags, and note after saving generally.
decisions.note: Specification gate: general bookmark editing was omitted from the purportedly complete scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 declared the scope complete without deletion. Client entry 26 required permanent deletion.
decisions.note: Specification gate: delete was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 declared the goal covered without archive behavior. Client entry 26 requested a reversible archive, hidden from normal collection/search and clearly distinct from permanent deletion.
decisions.note: Specification gate: archive semantics and its distinction from delete were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 omitted an archive view. Client entry 26 required archived bookmarks to “have their own view” and be restorable.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the archived-only list was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 declared coverage complete without multi-selection. Client entry 26 requested selecting several bookmarks for tag, read/unread, archive, and delete actions.
decisions.note: Specification gate: bulk actions on selected bookmarks were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 omitted collection-wide filtered actions. Client entry 26 required the same actions to apply optionally to every bookmark matching the current search, tag, or view.
decisions.note: Specification gate: apply-to-all-matching was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 summarized an optional note but no rendered formatting. Client entry 26 required notes to support and display simple formatting.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Markdown note rendering was explicitly added after being absent from the declared complete scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 omitted preserved copies. Client entry 26 required a preserved page copy and specified that PDF links preserve the PDF itself.
decisions.note: Specification gate: local preservation and the PDF rule were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 omitted Internet Archive support. Client entry 26 requested an option to send a bookmark to the Internet Archive.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Internet Archive preservation was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 omitted saved filters. Client entry 26 requested saving combinations of a search and included/excluded tags for reuse.
decisions.note: Specification gate: bundles/saved filters were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 omitted import. Client entry 26 required importing standard browser-bookmarks HTML while retaining titles, tags, and original dates.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Netscape HTML import was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 omitted export. Client entry 26 required exporting a standard browser-bookmarks HTML file.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Netscape HTML export was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 25/round 13 explicitly deferred control over displayed item count and omitted text-size settings. Client entry 26 reversed the deferral: item count must be in this build, alongside default sort and text size.
decisions.note: Specification gate: this revised decision superseded the earlier accepted deferral and restored the reference-conforming display settings to the build.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 presented editing address, title, description, tags, and note after saving. Client entry 28 approved the management flow.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: full bookmark editing conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 presented permanent deletion with confirmation and contrasted it with the coming reversible archive. Client entry 28 approved this distinction.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: permanent deletion and its distinction from archive conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 27/round 14 presented opening the original page by clicking the card, with tags and controls retaining their actions. Client entry 28 said this felt natural.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: selecting a list item navigates to the original URL.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 presented archive removing an item from All and ordinary search while preserving it for restoration. Client entry 30 confirmed complete separation and restoration.
decisions.note: Archive prototype: reversible hiding from default/search conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 stated “Archive = out of the way but safe and reversible; Delete = permanently gone.” Client entry 30 said the distinction was clear.
decisions.note: Archive prototype: archive and delete are properly distinguished.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 presented a separate Archived tab with restore. Client entry 30 approved the archived-only view.
decisions.note: Archive prototype: separate archived list conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 31/round 16 presented checkbox selection and bulk add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, delete, and restore. Client entry 32 said everything else in the multi-select flow matched.
decisions.note: Bulk-action prototype: selected-item actions conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 31/round 16 presented “Select all N matching” scoped to search, tag, and active tab. Client entry 32 called the current filtered view “exactly the right boundary.”
decisions.note: Bulk-action prototype: whole-filter actions conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 31/round 16 presented bulk tag add/remove as a quick type-in box and asked whether suggestions were wanted. Client entry 32 requested “existing-tag suggestions to the bulk add and remove boxes.”
decisions.note: Bulk-action prototype: tag entry in the bulk controls initially omitted autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 33/round 17 limited rendered Markdown to bold, italic, inline code, bullets, and links. Client entry 34 required headings, numbered lists, and quotes as well.
decisions.note: Formatted-note review: the presented Markdown subset was incomplete.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 35/round 18 presented rendering headings, numbered lists, quotes, bold, italic, code, and links, with direct syntax still supported. Client entry 36 confirmed the expanded set matched.
decisions.note: Revised formatted-note prototype conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 37/round 19 described an ordinary-page “Preserved copy”/snapshot but did not specify the required storage format. Client entry 38 supplied it: “a single self-contained HTML file.”
decisions.note: Preservation-flow review: the local HTML snapshot format was omitted from the presented behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 37/round 19 presented PDF links as preserving “the PDF itself.” Client entry 38 explicitly confirmed storing the PDF itself.
decisions.note: Preservation-flow review: PDF handling conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 37/round 19 presented a separate Internet Archive submission producing a public archive link. Client entry 38 approved keeping this separate from private preservation.
decisions.note: Preservation-flow review: Internet Archive support conforms; the requested public-copy confirmation is an additional safety preference.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 39/round 20 presented named, persistent filters containing search and included/excluded tags encoded through the search expression and active tag. Client entry 40 retained search text plus included and excluded tags, preferring dedicated pickers for understandability.
decisions.note: Saved-filter review: encoding tag conditions through the equivalent search language is not itself a divergence; the picker request is an implementation preference.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 39/round 20 made the saved filter remember “which tab you’re on.” Client entry 40 rejected that: “I would not include the current All, Read later, or Archived tab in it” and required applying the same subject filter within an appropriate view.
decisions.note: Saved-filter review: binding a bundle to a current perspective diverged from the reference bundle fields.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 41/round 21 presented standard bookmarks-file import preserving titles, tags, descriptions, and original dates. Client entry 42 approved the round-trip and preservation behavior.
decisions.note: Data-management prototype: Netscape HTML import conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 41/round 21 presented downloading a standard `bookmarks.html` export. Client entry 42 required archived items remain included and otherwise approved it; entry 43/round 22 presented the archived folder adjustment.
decisions.note: Linked data-management review: standard HTML export conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 43/round 22 presented remembered default sort, items shown per page, and text size. Client entry 44 confirmed all display preferences matched.
decisions.note: Final specification gate: the required display settings conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 45/round 23 reported implemented saving with real page metadata, editable title/description, tags with suggestions, formatted notes, read-later status, and duplicate convergence. Client entry 46 accepted the delivered application.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the recorded saving implementation claim conforms; this classification does not independently infer execution beyond the presentation.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 45/round 23 reported full-field search with #tag, phrases, Boolean operators, parentheses, tag browsing combined with search, and remembered sorting. Client entry 46 accepted the report.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the recorded retrieval implementation claim conforms; case-insensitive matching remains separately unresolved because it was not explicitly reported.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 45/round 23 reported a separate read-later view where marking read removes an item from that view but keeps it in the collection. Client entry 46 accepted it.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the recorded read-state implementation claim conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 45/round 23 reported full editing, permanent deletion, opening cards, archive/restore, selected-item actions, and all-matching actions. Client entry 46 accepted the report.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the recorded management implementation claim conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 45/round 23 reported real self-contained page/PDF preservation and separate confirmed public Internet Archive submission. Client entry 46 explicitly accepted “the real preservation and Internet Archive flows.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the recorded preservation implementation claim conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 45/round 23 reported named search plus include/exclude-tag filters and standard import/export preserving archived status without overwriting existing details. Client entry 46 accepted the application.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the recorded filter and data-transfer implementation claim conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 45/round 23 reported remembered default sort, items per page, and text size in Settings. Client entry 46 accepted the application.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the recorded settings implementation claim conforms.
